functions.desc: Shared non-blocking flock bracketed by human_holds() checks; yields for the callback lifetime

functions.name: drain

features.title: Teammate lifecycle and provisioning
features.purpose: Owner (and, with approval, manager bots) create, edit, clone, archive, restore, start, stop and delete persistent teammates. Every change becomes an immutable bot_operations snapshot that the worker drives through the Docker-owning supervisor, which (re)creates a hardened per-bot container with private network and volumes. UI shows provisioning/error/active status and allows retry.

logic.step: Owner mutation routes require Idempotency-Key; registry.mutation takes advisory lock on the key and replays/409s via owner_receipts.
validate_config resolves default provider/model, enforces permitted tools, skill names, and 'skills' tool for enabled skills.

register: global advisory lock 887832102, max_bots, id bot-<16hex>, generate bot token + runtime key (Fernet-encrypted, token sha256-hashed), runtime_url http://hermbot-bot-<id>:8642, DM conversation.
reserve_lifecycle fences: human computer control, pending op (incl as clone source), uncertain work; busy work requires interrupt and is cancelled.
owner_operation sets desired_state (stopped for stop/archive/delete), revision+1; delete needs exact name; restore only archived; archived bots can't start/stop.
enqueue snapshots configuration, revision, provider (with secret_encrypted), timezone, desired_state, previous_status, encrypted creds; status -> provisioning|deleting; readiness cleared.
Worker loop: queue_initial bootstraps 'ensure' for active bots with applied_revision<revision; claim leases ops 120 s; drive each.
drive waits while the bot (or clone source) has active/reserved attempts; cancels proposal-backed queued ops whose task/grant ended; marks applying; decrypts and POSTs RuntimeSpec to supervisor.
Supervisor operate: per-bot thread lock, receipt replay by operation_id with request_hash check, execute, fsync receipt + dir, cleanup clone helper.
execute_operation: stop/archive stop the container; delete removes container, helpers, owned volumes and dynamic network; others ensure (clone first when action clone).
ensure: create/verify volumes+network, connect api/worker, fingerprint; recreate container with env/labels/binds/limits/healthcheck; start and wait healthy (75 s).
On success bots.status active/archived/deleted with applied_revision=revision; delete nulls credentials and removes participants; events emitted.
On HTTP failure op failed, bot error with reason; transport errors keep op applying for re-drive.
Owner retry of failed op re-checks revision, busy work, clone source revision and live manager authority without consuming creation budget.
worker.probe every 20 iterations reconciles networks and refreshes readiness; dispatch requires readiness.compatible.

data.text: bots: status, desired_state, revision, applied_revision, runtime_error, readiness, config, encrypted credentials
bot_operations: action, status, payload snapshot, request_key unique, worker lease, proposal_id; one open per bot
Supervisor receipts receipts/<operation_id>.json {request_hash, result} on supervisor-state volume

decisions.decision: Only the supervisor holds the Docker socket; API/worker request lifecycle via an authenticated narrow HTTP API with server-owned names/images/mounts.
decisions.why: Contain Docker root-equivalent power to one small service.
decisions.alternatives: Mount docker.sock in api/worker; use compose for dynamic bots.
decisions.tradeoffs: Extra hop, single supervisor instance; secrets transit worker->supervisor.

decisions.decision: Durable outbox with immutable payload snapshot and leased workers.
decisions.why: Approved snapshots survive worker restart and replay exactly.

decisions.decision: Supervisor receipt files fsynced on a dedicated volume keyed by operation_id with request hash.
decisions.why: A lost receipt must not repeat a completed lifecycle effect (P2-08).

decisions.decision: Wait for Docker health before reporting success.
decisions.why: Provisioning previously reported success for failing runtimes (P2-05).

decisions.decision: Reuse the compose-created volumes/networks for the three core bots under supervisor management.

flows.title: Manager lifecycle proposal > owner approval > supervisor outbox > provisioning > manager resumes
flows.summary: A manager bot holding a grant proposes create/configure/start/stop; the owner approves the exact snapshot; the decision enqueues a bot_operation that the worker drives through the supervisor; the manager task resumes with a continuation once provisioning settles.

steps.text: Owner issues authority: standing grant (POST /api/v1/grants) or a task grant created with the task.
Manager model calls hermbot_propose; plugin forwards to /internal/tools with framework tool_call_id as receipt.

lifecycle.prepare checks grant authority/targets/creation budget, assigns server id for create, validates full config within grant resource limits, rejects busy targets without interrupt and uncertain work, freezes provider revision and affected tasks.
lifecycle.propose inserts approvals(kind lifecycle, payload hash, expiry) and lifecycle_proposals(pending); task -> waiting_approval; manager told to end turn.
Optionally owner edits: PUT /api/v1/proposals/{id} supersedes old proposal, stales approval, re-proposes.
Owner approves via POST /api/v1/approvals/{id} with expected_payload_hash; expiry/task-stopped/grant rechecked.

lifecycle.decide: deny -> proposal denied + resume. Approve -> recheck authority and provider revision; create: group <=6, register bot, grant created_bots+1 and target appended, participant added; else bot NOWAIT lock, expected revision, identical affected tasks, reserve_lifecycle, apply config or desired_state.
registry.enqueue(key proposal:<id>, proposal_id) creates bot_operations(queued) snapshot; proposal -> queued with operation_id; bots.status provisioning.
Worker loop claims op (120 s lease), drive waits for idle bot, re-checks the manager task and grant before dispatch (else cancels op, bot error, proposal cancelled), marks op and proposal applying.
drive decrypts provider key, bot token, runtime key and POSTs RuntimeSpec to supervisor /operations/{action} with SUPERVISOR_TOKEN.
Supervisor: per-bot lock, receipt replay or execute ensure: volumes/network, connect api/worker, create hardened hermbot-bot-<id>, start, wait healthy; write fsynced receipt.

Success: op completed, bot status active (or archived/deleted), applied_revision set, readiness cleared; proposal completed; lifecycle.resume appends continuation (bot id/action/state, use hermbot_teammates) and requeues the manager task.
Failure: op failed, bot error, proposal failed, manager resumed with failure text; transport loss leaves op applying for re-drive.
Probe refreshes readiness (networks reconcile + capabilities); new bot becomes dispatchable; resumed manager attempt dispatched by claim_new.

flows.title: Login, session and owner authentication
flows.summary: Owner pastes OWNER_TOKEN once; the API mints an opaque HttpOnly session cookie whose hash is stored; every owner request/WebSocket is verified against the bearer or the cookie hash; logout and session revocation are explicit.

steps.text: Compose requires OWNER_TOKEN; api lifespan refuses any service secret shorter than 32 chars.
UI POSTs /api/v1/session with Authorization Bearer token.
auth.verify compares bearer with compare_digest.
auth.login creates token_urlsafe(32), stores sha256 in owner_sessions with 1-day expiry and sets hermbot_session cookie HttpOnly SameSite=Strict (Secure if https).
Later requests: owner dependency verifies cookie hash not revoked/expired; middleware rejects cross-origin non-GET.
WebSocket computer stream: Origin==Host, verify, re-verify every 5 s.
Owner can list and revoke sessions by hash.
Logout revokes current session, signs out push device, deletes cookies.
Bots authenticate separately with HERMBOT_BOT_TOKEN hash lookup.

flows.title: Bot create / clone / delete provisioning path
flows.summary: Owner lifecycle requests become bot_operations snapshots driven by the worker through the supervisor; clone uses a helper container; delete removes runtime and private volumes but keeps history.

steps.text: Create: POST /api/v1/bots (Idempotency-Key) -> validate_config -> register (lock, max_bots, id, credentials, DM) -> enqueue 'create'.
Clone: POST /bots/{id}/clone -> roster lock, source revision check, reserve source, register target, enqueue 'clone' with source_bot_id, source_revision, source_was_running, copy_options.
Worker drives op; skips while target or clone source has active attempts.

Supervisor ensure(clone=True): clone_state validates options/ownership, stops source, runs hermbot-clone-<op> (root, no network, source ro, target rw) executing copy_state.py, waits, restarts source if it was running; then creates runtime; cleanup_clone removes helper.
copy_state copies memory/skills/workspace and history via SQLite backup; skips symlinks and credential/config names; browser volume never copied.
Runtime container start triggers hermes_bootstrap and health checks on 8642/8643.
Delete: POST /bots/{id}/delete with exact-name confirmation -> desired stopped, enqueue delete, status deleting (bot token rejected).
Supervisor delete removes container, clone helpers, owned volumes and dynamic network (disconnecting api/worker).
Completion: status deleted, credentials nulled, participants removed; conversations remain as Past teammates.

flows.title: Attachment upload > MinIO > install into bot workspace
flows.summary: Owner uploads base64 file to a conversation; bytes stored in MinIO with sha256; before each native run the worker reads (verifying checksum) and the supervisor installs them into /workspace/attachments/<id>/<name> via root exec staging and write_attachment.py.

steps.text: UI POST /api/v1/conversations/{id}/attachments with Idempotency-Key.
Validate ASCII plain name, MIME allowlist, strict base64, 1 B..10 MB; compute sha256.
put_object to bucket hermbot key attachments/<conv>/<id> with sha metadata; insert attachments row (idempotent receipt).
Owner message/task carries attachment_ids (tasks.attachment_ids).
Worker drive (before native start, no human control) calls provisioning.copy_attachments: attachments + artifacts granted to the task.
ArtifactStore.read_bytes verifies size and sha256; POST supervisor /attachments with base64.

Supervisor validates filename, base64, size and checksum, finds runtime, then under the per-bot lock: STAGING_INIT, 60 000-byte STAGING_WRITE chunks, exec write_attachment.py, all as root via docker exec.
write_attachment.install re-validates, walks /workspace with O_NOFOLLOW dir fds, writes temp O_EXCL, fsync, chown hermes, atomic replace; staging unlinked.
Bot reads /workspace/attachments/<id>/<name>; owner can download via GET /api/v1/attachments/{id}.

flows.title: Stack startup sequence
flows.summary: Compose orders postgres (healthy) and storage (started) before api; api initializes DB under an advisory lock, runs schema+migrations, seeds core bots, bootstraps credentials and creates the bucket; worker waits for api health and the runtime image build, then bootstraps 'ensure' operations that make the supervisor create runtime containers, whose bootstrap starts the adapter and Hermes gateway.

steps.text: runtime-image service builds hermbot-hermes:phase4 and exits 0 (network none).
postgres healthy via pg_isready; storage started (no healthcheck); supervisor starts independently (no depends_on).
api starts after postgres healthy and storage started.

api lifespan: secret length check; db.initialize: open pool, advisory xact lock 887832101, run schema.sql then sorted migrations, seed Scout/Quill/Sage with runtime_url http://hermes-<id>:8642 and DMs, registry.bootstrap (env provider import, per-bot credentials).
ArtifactStore.initialize creates bucket 'hermbot' if missing.
api healthcheck /health runs SELECT 1.
worker (after api healthy and runtime-image completed) and event/notification workers (after api healthy) also run db.initialize serialized by the advisory lock.

Worker loop: queue_initial enqueues 'ensure' for active bots with applied_revision < revision (fresh seeds have 1 > 0); drive -> supervisor creates hermbot-bot-<id> (migrating any legacy compose container found by find_runtime).
Runtime bootstrap: install read-only plugin, drop to hermes, clean Chromium markers, write config.yaml/SOUL.md, validate skills, spawn adapter 8643, exec Hermes gateway 8642.
Supervisor waits for container health; worker probe stores readiness; dispatch enabled for compatible bots. Restart: runtimes restart unless-stopped; worker reconciles networks.

discrepancies.text: INTERNAL_TOKEN is mandatory in compose and length-checked at startup, but the app.internal() dependency that verifies it is never used by any route.
plugin.yaml provides_tools lists 19 tools and omits hermbot_ask, hermbot_work_status and hermbot_publish_file that __init__.py registers (22) and runtime readiness requires (all ARGUMENT_MODELS).

Legacy-profile hermes-* services cannot pass current readiness: no HERMBOT_ADAPTER_KEY (adapter rejects all authenticated calls), no BOT_ID (routine scheduler KeyError), no browser-state volume, healthcheck only 8642; README says retained for migration reference only.

bot_operations status 'uncertain' is referenced (unique index, pending checks) but never written; ambiguous transport leaves 'applying' and is re-driven after lease expiry. README describes it as 'remains in reconciliation'.
Version labels are inconsistent: app image tag hermbot-app:phase1, /health phase 4, FastAPI version 0.4.0, pyproject 0.1.0, plugin 0.5.0 (README acknowledges historical phase1 names).
PHASE3.md says the runtime image is hermbot-hermes:phase3; code/compose use phase4 (historical doc).
SKILLS-TOOLS-REVIEW records an 18-tool contract and adapter version 3; code now requires adapter 4 and registers 22 tools.
Root files diagnostic.py and final_upgrade.py are empty (0 bytes) and unreferenced.
README states desktop startup requires 1,536 MB free but also that the default desktop memory floor is 1,024 MB; bootstrap default min_free_memory_mb is 1024.
PHASE3-REVIEW claims one plain-filename contract across upload/transport/installation, but conversation attachment upload uses an ASCII-only regex and narrower MIME list than library filename().

Clone skip-list applies to every path component, so any workspace/skill file named config.yaml, token, tokens or plugins is silently not cloned (README: 'known credential/configuration files are excluded').
README claims pinned toolchain; runtime image apt packages (chromium, tigervnc, xfce) are unpinned.
Brief/assumption 'runtime port 8642': 8642 is the native Hermes API server; Hermbot's runtime_api adapter listens on 8643. No VNC TCP port exists (RFB over unix socket).

compose.protocol.yaml overrides only api/worker/legacy runtimes; managed hermbot-bot-* get the fixture via the imported Environment provider (bootstrap) — README restricts protocol tests to the initial roster.
Clone helper container lacks the runtime hardening (runs as root without read-only rootfs/cap-drop/no-new-privileges), mitigated by NetworkMode none.
Capabilities route types bot_id as plain str (no BotId pattern) unlike other bot routes.

topology.text: Compose project 'hermbot': postgres, storage (MinIO), api, worker, event-worker, notification-worker, supervisor, runtime-image build helper; legacy hermes-* under profile 'legacy'; model-fixture only with compose.protocol.yaml. Dynamic hermbot-bot-<id> runtimes and hermbot-clone-<op> helpers are created by the supervisor, not compose.
Networks: control (postgres, storage, api, worker, both workers, supervisor); one bridge network per bot (runtime + api + worker). Only host port 127.0.0.1:8780->api:8000.
Each runtime serves Hermes native API (8642) and Hermbot adapter (8643); calls back to api:8000 /internal with its bot token.

control-vs-data-plane.text: Control plane: api/worker decide; supervisor alone mutates Docker (create/stop/delete/exec) via narrow authenticated API; desired_state/revision recorded in PostgreSQL.
Data plane: Hermes runs execute inside runtimes; bytes move through MinIO (artifacts/attachments), adapter export, supervisor attachment exec, and RFB WebSocket relays.

isolation.text: Per-bot container, network, identity and data/workspace/browser volumes; bots cannot reach postgres, storage, supervisor or other bots (not on their networks).

Runtime hardening: read-only rootfs, no-new-privileges, cap_drop ALL with CHOWN/DAC_OVERRIDE/FOWNER/SETGID/SETUID only for bootstrap, tmpfs /tmp,/run,/opt/data/plugins, init, memory/CPU limits; bootstrap drops to hermes uid; plugin dir root-owned read-only.
Docker socket only in supervisor (runs as root); app containers run as uid 10001; event/notification workers read-only with small tmpfs and limits.

Isolation is a trusted single-owner container boundary, not hostile-code OS isolation; bots have outbound egress (bridge networks) and can read their own env secrets (model key, runtime key, bot token).

security.text: Distinct credentials: OWNER_TOKEN, session cookies (hash-stored), SUPERVISOR_TOKEN, per-bot bot token (hash lookup) and runtime key (Bearer to 8642/8643), all compared with compare_digest or hash equality; CONFIG_ENCRYPTION_KEY Fernet-encrypts persisted provider keys and bot credentials.
Cookie HttpOnly+SameSite=Strict; Origin==Host check for non-GET and WebSockets; validation errors stripped of inputs; no-store/nosniff headers.
INTERNAL_TOKEN unused; MinIO used with root credentials; secrets in plaintext container env and worker->supervisor HTTP JSON.

recovery.text: Outbox + leases + supervisor receipts make provisioning replay-safe across worker/supervisor restarts.
Runtimes restart unless-stopped; worker probe reconnects api/worker to bot networks and restarts exited runtimes; supervisor-managed containers survive 'docker compose stop'.
Every service re-runs idempotent schema/migrations under an advisory lock at startup.

scaling-spof.text: Single supervisor with in-process per-bot locks and file receipts; single postgres and MinIO; single owner. Worker leases allow multiple workers for bot_operations.
One active attempt per bot (DB index) and max_concurrent_runs 1 in Hermes; workspace max_bots 3..30.

production-path.text: Linux staging/HTTPS deferred; cookie Secure only with https PUBLIC_URL.
Per-bot VM isolation proposed and deferred beyond the roadmap; keep supervisor/coordination/credentials outside guests; guest root changes trust in plugin/adapter.
